'Is ferrel-bound to' is not transitive..why: "Ferrel-bound" is a made-up relation (catalogued as ferrel_bound_to, fictional, no property tags): it is not a phrase anyone uses and its words carry no built-in sense of chaining, so a model has no default reading of it as transitive or not. The people in the instances (Florence Nightingale, Franz Schubert, Harriet Tubman, Mark Twain, Marie Curie, Mahatma Gandhi) are real but not known to be tied in any such way.

notes: RBox expansion paired with people-replace-0009 (which makes 'is an ancestor of' not transitive): a made-up relation, ferrel_bound_to, is given the same property, not transitive, applied to real people with no known link. Both ties are given in the prompt, so what follows is fixed by the edit alone; a chain of three unrelated people gives a model no family or social reading of the relation to lean on. Side facts and near and far unrelated queries are those of the revision record. Yes and no: the direct question, the cross-lingual queries and the first instance ask whether the chained tie follows (no), the second instance asks whether it could fail (yes). The negation asks whether the relation is transitive (no). hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as one bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do.
